note:
FIRQA — Cairo 1964. "Enta Omri", Umm Kulthum's first record with
Baligh Hamdi, premiered on the first Thursday of February 1964 and
famous for the thing this row is: a takht of five or six players
grown into an orchestra of massed violins, with an electric guitar
and a Farfisa organ in it, and a twelve-minute instrumental
introduction before the singer opens her mouth.
THE MAQAM IS KURD AND THAT IS WHY THIS ROW CAN SHIP. Enta Omri is in
maqam kurd, which is the phrygian mode note for note — no neutral
degree, nothing off the grid. The row above says which four maqamat
this box is locked out of; this one is simply not one of them, and
`MODES.phrygian` here is not the nearest-Western approximation that
`mahraganat` had to settle for, it is the right answer.
THE AXES: CAST is the identity. Thirty violins playing the SAME line
as the singer, an octave apart, not a harmony — and Development is
tarab, the line repeated and repeated with the ornament pushed
further each time until the hall shouts. The `word` schedule below
is that escalation and it is the closest thing in this table to an
audience.

LINEAGE: `taqsim` is the modal tradition the singer and every
instrumentalist grew up inside — the record still opens with one —
and `romantic` is named at a real weight for the same reason
`filmi` names it: a massed violin section with a conductor is a
nineteenth-century European institution, and the arrangers were
trained on it. That is not a resemblance, it is a debt.
REWRITTEN 2026-08-30 (the walls-down round; the old line read
`parents: { taqsim: 0.6, romantic: 0.4 }` and the wants opened
with "the takht"): `tarab` (Cairo 1934) is the singer's OWN
earlier era — the takht behind Umm Kulthum on the radio's first
night — so the takht debt is paid by the era that WAS the takht,
and taqsim's weight flows partly through it.
"muwashshah" PAID 2026-08-30 (Cairo 1200, Dar at-Tiraz — the
dated source the old decline said did not exist): Umm Kulthum's
repertory and the firqa's own concert form both keep the
strophic inheritance, and the edge finally says so.

THE WAHDA: dum on 1, tak on the and-of-2, dum on 3, tak on 4 —
four beats with the weight at the front, which is the rhythm a
long Umm Kulthum verse sits on. The `p` lane is the riq's
continuous jingle and it is a rim sample doing a tambourine's job.

WHO SINGS: `melisma` — one vowel held across many notes,
which is the literal description of what she does to a
line of Ahmad Shafiq Kamal's poetry

WEIGHTS RESCALED 2026-09-03 (the catalogue round, shift 3). This row's 4 declared shares summed to 1.10, and a row cannot be more than all of itself — the sum is a claim about how much of THIS record its named ancestors explain, so above 1 it is not a claim at all. Every RATIO here is the row's own and none of them moved; the total did, back onto the catalogue's own 0.05 grid: tarab .40→.35, taqsim .30→.25, romantic .30→.25. The row now attributes 0.95 of itself and keeps .05 as its own invention. Rescaling to 1 rather than to something smaller is the conservative reading on purpose: it credits this row with the SMALLEST invention consistent with what it already said, so no residue is asserted that nobody argued for. GENRES.md §2, `parents`.
label: Cairo 1964
cannot: heterophony — the violins play the singer's OWN line, slightly differently, at the same time; this table has `line` chairs that get their own operator word and `pad` chairs that voice chords, and 'the same tune, thirty times, imperfectly' is neither
the length — a tarab performance repeats a line as many times as the room asks for and runs an hour; the form here is fixed when the record compiles and nobody in it is listening
the riq and the darbuka — there is no hand drum among the kit samples, so the wahda is voiced on a kick and a rim, which is the same bol loss `filmi` declares
words: the singer, the line said again, further each time
the violins, thirty of them on her tune
the accordion, answering in the gaps

(v, s) => (v === 0 ? [[], [fill(2)], [fill(2), rotate(2)], [fill(4), rotate(5)]][s % 4]
                    : v === 1 ? [transpose(7), drop(2)]
                    : v === 2 ? [rotate(8), drop(4)]
                    : [drop(8)])
